To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a theory for Shapiro steps in tunnel junctions with spatial modulation of the critical current density, which is applicable to asymmetric grain boundaries in YBaCuO thin films and superconductor- ferromagnet-supercondutor heterostructures.

we theoretically studied Shapiro steps in Josephson tunnel junctions with spatial alternating critical current density and developed a coarse-graining theory for the asymmetric grain boundaries and superconductor- ferromagnet-superconducting heterostructures.

we derived an analytical formula for the width of Shapiro steps in Josephson tunnel junctions with spatial alternating critical current density and we developed a coarse-graining model for the analysis of Shapiro steps in superconductor- ferromagnet-super-conductor Josephson junctions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the theory of superconductivity in nanostructures, in particular, in the vicinity of superconductor-normal metal and superconductor- ferromagnet interfaces, and in the theory of Josephson junctions and Josephson junction arrays.
theoretical description of the effects caused by spatially alternating critical density in superconducting junctions.
the study of the Josephson effect in the presence of spatially varying current density and magnetic field in Josephson junction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Shapiro step width is proportional to the inverse of the critical current density.
the Josephson effect in SFS structures is a very promising and interesting phenomenon.

the Shapiro steps in the current-voltage curves of the asymmetric Josephson junctions are the result of the interplay between the spatial modulation of the critical current density and the spatial modulation of phase of the superconducting order parameter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the width of Shapiro steps in the asymmetric grain boundaries and superconductor- ferromagnet-superconducting junctions can be calculated from the width of Shapiro step in the symmetric junctions by the simple formula: W = W _{0} (1 + α ^{2} ), where W _{0} is the width of the Shapiro steps in the symmetric junction and α is the asymmetry coefficient of the junctions.
we have developed a theory of Shapiro steps in the current-voltage curves of Josephson junctions and heterostructures with spatially varying critical current density.
the alternating critical current density can be used as a new tool to study the physics of Josephson junctions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anomalous Shapiro step is always wider than its normal counterpart, which is consistent with the experimental observations in the literature.

the width of the anomalous Shapiro steps in the current-voltage characteristics is much larger than the corresponding width of the normal Shapiro steps, which can be used to identify the presence of alternating current density in Josephson junction.
the width of the half-integer Shapiro steps can be much smaller than the width of the integer steps in asymmetric grain boundaries and in S/F/S Josephson structures.
